changelog:
Add a very large playlist without the app running out of memory, and see what each refresh actually did.

WHAT CHANGED

- A playlist source is now read from a file on the phone rather than held in memory all at once, so a very large playlist no longer risks the app closing. While it loads, the progress line counts the entries read so far.
- Each source in Settings says what its last refresh did: how many channels, films and series it stored, what it kept from before and why, or why it stored nothing.
- When a refresh reads rows it does not keep, such as a channel listed twice or a playlist line with no usable link, the source says how many and why.
- The source row always shows when the subscription ends, as a date, and still warns you in the last two weeks. It also shows how many connections the provider allows.
- Scanning channels while something is playing now depends on your line. With two or more connections the scan runs and keeps one for what you are watching. With one, it still waits until you stop, and says why.
- Settings, Sources has a new setting for how long to wait for a provider's list, from 1 to 10 minutes. The default is still 3 minutes. Raise it if a slow provider's refresh keeps failing.
- With diagnostic mode on, the app keeps a copy of what the provider sent, up to 64 MB in total, to help with a problem report. Clear log removes them.

WHAT STAYS THE SAME

- A refresh still keeps your old catalog if the new one does not arrive whole.

NOT YET

- The app does not yet compare the rows it offered to the database with the rows the database kept, and a refresh still writes each source in one step.
